chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to cut [the hand of the thief] regarding a 'Bayza'. I said, 'And what is a Bayza?' He said, 'A Bayza, its value is a quarter of a Dinar.' And I said, 'Is it the lowest threshold for the Hadd [punishment] of the thief?' So he was silent.

key_terms.أَدْنَى حَدِّ: Adna al-Hadd: The lowest threshold or minimum limit for the legal punishment.
key_terms.السَّارِقِ: Al-Sariq: The thief, the subject of the Hadd punishment.
key_terms.بَيْضَة: Bayza: A specific unit of value or coinage, defined here as a quarter of a Dinar.
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: Rub' Dinar: A quarter of a Dinar, the specific monetary value assigned to the Bayza.

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for the Hadd punishment of cutting the hand in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the nisab (minimum value) for the Hadd punishment of cutting the thief's hand, identifying the 'Bayza' as a quarter of a Dinar. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms this specific valuation as the lower limit, and his silence in response to the questioner's inquiry signifies the finality and acceptance of this jurisprudential standard within Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Sama’at Bin Mahran, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws used to cut regrding a ‘Bayza’. I said, ‘And what is a ‘Bayza’ (a helmet)?’ Heasws said: ‘A Bayza, its value is a quarter Dinaar’. And I said, ‘Is it the lowest (value) for a Penalty (Hadd) of a thief?’ So heasws was silent (in agreement)’.
